top_categories.workout_context: 431 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
47,667ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
Tour of Nilgiris (TFN)'s mountain passes forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 431 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour of Nilgiris (TFN)'s demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before December.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 431 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
At Tour of Nilgiris (TFN), surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
47,667ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
111ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
431 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 47,667ft of climbing on mountain passes does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour of Nilgiris (TFN). Train it until it feels boring.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Tour of Nilgiris (TFN), that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 431 miles requires a practiced resupply plan built around confirmed course services and available commercial stops. Rehearse frequent carbohydrate intake on long rides, then scale the plan to intensity, sleep strategy, tolerance, and real food across the full event. Carry redundant fuel and avoid applying a short-event hourly target or fixed total-calorie estimate to a multi-day race.
race_overlay.altitude: Tour of Nilgiris (TFN) with 47,667ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Tour of Nilgiris (TFN) requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mountain passes to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, VO2max, and Road Specific to prepare you for 431 miles of mountain passes in Mysuru to Ooty via Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu, India.
